# Plan a Weekly Grocery List with Apple Intelligence

Ever wished your iPhone could magically figure out what groceries you need based on what you plan to eat? This guide will show you how to build a basic Siri Shortcut that, once Apple Intelligence is fully rolled out and enabled, can learn your meal preferences and intelligently help create your weekly shopping list, saving you time and mental effort.

## Before you start
- An iPhone running iOS 18 or later.
- The free Apple Shortcuts app installed (usually pre-installed).
- An Apple ID signed in to your iPhone.
- This guide assumes Apple Intelligence features will be enabled on your device when they become available.
- Rough total time: 10-15 minutes.

## Step 1 — Open the Shortcuts App
First, you need to find and open the Shortcuts app on your iPhone. This app is like a personal automation assistant, letting you create custom actions and link different apps together.
On your screen, look for an icon with two overlapping coloured squares, one blue and one purple, shaped like a flow chart symbol. It might be in a folder with other Apple apps or on your home screen. Tap this icon to open it. If you can’t find it, swipe down from the middle of your home screen to bring up the Search bar and type "Shortcuts."
You'll know it worked when the Shortcuts app opens, displaying a screen with "My Shortcuts" at the top and possibly a list of existing shortcuts or a prompt to create a new one.

## Step 2 — Start a New Shortcut
Now, let's begin building your custom grocery list helper. Creating a new shortcut gives you a blank canvas to design your automated task.
At the top-right corner of the "My Shortcuts" screen, you'll see a small plus sign (+) icon. Tap this icon. A new screen will appear titled "New Shortcut" or "Add Action," showing a search bar and a list of suggested actions. This is where you'll choose what your shortcut does.
You'll know it worked when you see the "New Shortcut" screen, ready for you to add your first action.

## Step 3 — Add Actions to Capture Meal Ideas
To "learn" your meals, the shortcut needs a way for you to easily record them. We'll start by adding actions that let you input your meal plan for the week.
On the "New Shortcut" screen, tap the "Add Action" button or use the search bar at the top to look for actions. First, search for "Ask for Input" and tap it to add it to your shortcut. Next, search for "Add to Reminders" and tap it. Repeat this for "Choose from Menu" and "Text". Drag these actions into order. Set the "Ask for Input" prompt to something like "What are you planning to eat this week?" and set its type to "Text." Then, connect the text output to the "Add to Reminders" action, placing it in a "Weekly Meals" list (or create one). The "Choose from Menu" can offer common meals.
💬 Example: `What are you planning to eat this week?`
If it looks different: If you don't see "Add to Reminders," look for "Create Reminder" or "Add to Notes" instead. You can always change the list later.
You'll know it worked when your shortcut screen shows a sequence of actions, starting with "Ask for Input" and then "Add to Reminders" or "Add to Notes," ready to capture your meal ideas.

## Step 4 — Add Actions to Compile a Basic List
Next, we'll build the basic structure for creating your grocery list. This part of the shortcut will gather information and start putting items onto a designated grocery list.
In the "Add Action" search bar, type "Find Reminders." Tap it to add. Then, tap on "Add filter" and set it to find reminders in your "Weekly Meals" list (the one you set up in Step 3). This tells the shortcut to look at your meal plans. Below this, add another action by searching for "Text," then type a general grocery item, like "Milk" or "Bread," into the text box. Finally, search for "Add to Reminders" again, and set it to add to your "Grocery List."
💬 Example: (in the "Text" action): `Milk, Bread, Eggs`
If it looks different: Ensure your "Grocery List" exists in the Reminders app beforehand, or the shortcut might create a new one each time.
You'll know it worked when your shortcut now has actions to find your weekly meal ideas and then adds some basic grocery items to your main "Grocery List."

## Step 5 — Refine and Anticipate Apple Intelligence
This is where your shortcut gets smart. While Apple Intelligence isn't fully released, we'll design this shortcut to be ready for its powerful capabilities. Instead of you manually listing every ingredient, Apple Intelligence will eventually learn from your meal inputs and automatically suggest the right items.
Back in your shortcut, after the "Find Reminders" action, you would typically add many "Text" and "Add to Reminders" actions for each ingredient. However, once Apple Intelligence is active, Siri will intelligently process the text from your "Weekly Meals" reminders. It will be able to interpret "Spaghetti Bolognese" and suggest "pasta, mince, tomatoes, onion." Add a "Show Alert" action and type a message anticipating this.
💬 Example: (in "Show Alert" text): `Your Apple Intelligence-enhanced Siri will soon suggest ingredients here!`
If it looks different: You might need to experiment with different "Text" inputs for now. Once Apple Intelligence is available, you'll look for settings within Siri or Shortcuts that enable intelligent suggestions based on your logged meals.
You'll know it worked when your shortcut includes a "Show Alert" action, acknowledging the future integration of Apple Intelligence, which will transform your manual input into intelligent suggestions.

## Step 6 — Name and Test Your Shortcut
You've built the framework for your smart grocery list! Now, give it a clear name and run it for the first time to see it in action.
From the "New Shortcut" or current shortcut editing screen, tap the small down arrow or "New Shortcut" text at the very top. A menu will appear with options like "Rename," "Duplicate," or "Details." Tap "Rename." Type a descriptive name, like "Weekly Grocery Helper," then tap "Done." To test, tap the small play button (triangle icon) at the bottom-right of the screen. The shortcut will run, asking for your meal input and adding items to your lists.
💬 Example: `Weekly Grocery Helper`
If it looks different: The "Rename" option might be under a "…" (ellipsis) icon in some versions.
You'll know it worked when your shortcut has a new name, and when you tap the play button, it prompts you for your meal ideas and then confirms items have been added to your Reminders lists.

## Common mistakes
- **Forgetting to create your "Weekly Meals" and "Grocery List" in Reminders beforehand:** The shortcut might create new lists each time it runs, or add items to your general 'Reminders' list instead of a specific one. Always set up your lists in the Reminders app first.
- **Over-complicating it initially:** Don't try to add every single ingredient for every meal at first. Start with general meal ideas and common staples. As Apple Intelligence evolves, it will fill in the gaps for you.
- **Not knowing where to find the Shortcuts app:** If it's not on your home screen, remember to swipe down and use the search bar to locate it quickly.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Imagine less stress about meal planning. Your phone will get smarter at understanding your preferences, suggesting ingredients, and proactively helping you build a shopping list, freeing up your mental energy for other things.
- **For your business or work:** While this example is personal, the ability of Apple Intelligence to learn patterns and suggest actions can extend to work tasks. Think about shortcuts that learn your routine meetings and suggest relevant documents, or help categorise emails.
- **If you're just getting started:** The easiest first move is to simply create the "Weekly Grocery Helper" shortcut and get used to inputting your meal ideas. Even without full Apple Intelligence integration yet, having a dedicated place to log your meal plans is a great start.

## Try it now
Open the Shortcuts app, tap the '+' to start a new shortcut, and add the "Ask for Input" action. Set the prompt to "What's for dinner tonight?" and tap the play button to see it in action!
